thread:
Ava: flagging a few things from today's design review of the autoscale SLO card. main ask: can we surface the estimated cost delta inline when users change min/max or enable burst? screenshot: https://redwood.app/s/ux/22678
Ravi: +1. cost feedback is crucial. if we show a tiny inline chip that updates to show +$0.12/hr it helps teams make tradeoffs quickly.
Jun: careful with noise. we could show cost only when values change (transient toast-like chip) instead of permanent label. avoids clutter in stable state.
Maya: accessibility reminder: tooltips and transient chips must be keyboard accessible and persistent long enough for SR users. aria-live region could announce new cost.
Noor: agree. aria-live="polite" for the estimated cost and an `aria-label` that reads "Estimated cost change: plus twelve cents per hour". also ensure color contrast on the chip meets 4.5:1.
Ava: another item: the pool selector is currently to the right of the slider. people suggested moving it left so keyboard flow matches visual reading order on compact cards.
Ravi: moving DOM order might break other cards that assume pool on the right. alternative: keep DOM but visually reorder with CSS `order` so the DOM order (slider, pool) stays logical for SR users.
Jun: visual reordering via CSS is fine, but test with VoiceOver — sometimes SR announces based on visual placement. prefer keeping DOM == visual when possible.
Maya: microcopy tweak: helper under the slider says "SLO target". Suggest change to "target latency SLO (ms)" to clarify units.
Noor: also add guardrail inline messaging: when max > 8 GPUs show a subtle amber hint "High throughput — consider Dedicated capacity" with a link to docs. ensure it's `role=status` and keyboard focusable link.
Ava: sync decisions: 1) transient cost chip appears when values change (aria-live) 2) try CSS reorder for pool left on compact, but keep DOM order if SR issues appear 3) change helper copy to include units 4) add guardrail hint when max > 8.
design-bot: created branch feature/slo-inline-cost-22678 and uploaded mock slo_inline_cost.png
Jun: i'll prototype the transient chip implementation and test SR announcement. aiming to push a prototype by EOD.
Ravi: i'll run a quick contrast and keyboard flow test on the prototype once ready.
Noor: i'll own the accessibility sign-off; please ping me when branch is ready.
Ava: cool. i'll update the product doc with the microtest scenarios and add the guardrail copy in the spec.
Maya: thanks all 44d
